What number is missing from the boxes in the statement below?

The ratio of triangles to hexagons is $1:\boxed{}\,$ because there is $1$ triangle for every $\boxed{}$ hexagon.
question.worked_solution:
First, we count the number of triangles. We see that there are $3$ triangles.

Then, we count the number of hexagons. We see that there are $3$ hexagons.

So the ratio of triangles to hexagons is $3:3.$

We can simplify this ratio by dividing both numbers by $3$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\,\,3 &  & : & \,\,\,\, & \,\,\,3 &  \\ \,\,↓÷\,\,3 &  &  &  & \,\,\,↓÷\,\,3 &  \\ \,\,1 &  & : &  & \,\,\,1 & \end{aligned}
$$

This means that $1:1$ is equivalent to $3:3.$ 

So, the complete statement is
"The ratio of triangles to hexagons is $1:1$ because there is $1$ triangle for every $1$ hexagon."
